title: item_cachedump's headroom guard reserves five bytes for "END\r\n" while the marker is written with a terminating NUL, so the NUL lands one byte past the buffer
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: the guard is `bufcurr + len + 5 > memlimit` and "END\r\n" is five characters, but the marker is written with a terminating NUL because the buffer is returned as a C string; six bytes are needed, so an entry landing bufcurr at memlimit-5 passes and the NUL lands at offset memlimit
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc, no slab or cache layer in between. Nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED.
nested_why: nothing sub-allocated the crossed region: the object is one allocation the platform's malloc handed out directly, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. The platform's own malloc/free. memlimit is reduced to 64 -- a size class, deliberately, so the CheriBSD prediction is not confounded by allocator slack -- and the entry length is chosen to land bufcurr exactly at memlimit-5, which is the reachable worst case the guard admits. The case ASSERTS that the entry is admitted and the terminator crosses at the pin, and rejected under the fix, so a reduction with the wrong arithmetic fails rather than reporting a verdict about nothing. sprintf/strcpy are reduced to the write they perform; nothing about WHERE the NUL lands is reduced, because that is the defect.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source, not from ancestry, and keyed on the identifier: 1.6.45:items.c contains the FIXED headroom (`+ 6 > memlimit` / `6 is END\r\n\0`) 1 time and the pre-fix form (`+ 5 > memlimit` / `5 is END\r\n`) 0 times. Two-sided, so the probe is known to fire. A fix-reversal; the convention is at ../allocator-repros/README.md:132-135.
distinguishing: the only row in this corpus whose crossing is a TERMINATOR rather than payload -- the guard's constant counts a marker's characters and forgets the NUL that makes it a C string. Case 0's crossing is also a terminating NUL, but there the size argument itself was wrong (sb.st_size rather than +1); here the size is right and the RESERVED HEADROOM is one short, which is a different error in a different place. Both are one-term reversals and they are not duplicates.
citation_constraint: the upstream fix is cited by HASH ONLY, deliberately. Its subject line names an outside contributor, and a person's name must not enter a committed file in this tree. docs/ref/memcached-spatial-defect-triage.md:43-45 records the same constraint against this hash, which is why the row was easy to miss.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle:
MEASURED 2026-10-07, results/20261007-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT**, CONFIRMING this arm's prediction. signal=34 (SIGPROT), si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102458, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x102440` from the ELF independently -- the fault lies INSIDE the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the range is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. THE PREDICTION'S CONDITION HELD, and that is the finding: the request is 64 bytes, which IS a size class, so CheriBSD's malloc leaves no slack and the one-byte crossing leaves the USABLE allocation. Case 0 of this same corpus crosses by one byte too and is NOT caught, because its 9-byte request yields a 16-byte capability. So the usable-size mechanism is now measured at two points inside one corpus -- one refuting a catch prediction, one confirming it -- rather than argued from a single reading. 6 of 6 arms, runner exit 0, both platform controls firing in the same boot.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 in the same vehicle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102480, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x102468` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.
